scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: SUPPORT & RESISTANCE: ROLE REVERSAL, ROUND NUMBERS & RETRACEMENTS

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. The Principle of Polarity. A broken support level becomes a formidable future resistance ceiling; a decisively broken resistance level becomes an authoritative future support floor.
beats.en_subtitle: Pillar one: 1. The Principle of Polarity. A broken support level becomes a formidable future resistance ceiling; a decisively broken resistance level becomes an authoritative future support floor.

cards.title: 1. The Principle of Polarity
cards.desc: A broken support level becomes a formidable future resistance ceiling; a decisively broken resistance level becomes an authoritative future support floor.

cards.title: 2. The Three-Cohort Psychology
cards.desc: At support, longs want to add, shorts regret not covering, and sideline cash waits to enter; upon breakdown, all three cohorts become desperate sellers.

cards.title: 3. Round Number Psychological Barriers
cards.desc: Market participants naturally anchor stop orders, profit targets, and mental limits at round numbers like $50, $100, ₹1000, creating self-fulfilling zones.

cards.title: 4. Percentage Retracement Ratios
cards.desc: Countertrend pullbacks predictably retrace calculable geometric proportions of the prior wave: 33%, 38.2%, 50%, and 61.8% (Fibonacci/Dow).

ui_state.question: A stock traded between a horizontal support floor of ₹200 and a resistance ceiling of ₹240 for six months before decisively breaking below ₹200 on heavy volume to ₹175. Weeks later, the stock rallies back up to touch ₹198. How should a technician apply Murphy's Principle of Polarity?
options: A) Buy aggressively because the stock is about to break back into its former range.
B) Expect former support at ₹200 to act as a formidable new resistance ceiling where trapped buyers will sell to break even.
C) Ignore the ₹200 level because prior price history is deleted after a breakdown.
D) Polarity only applies in commodity markets, not equity stocks.

options: A) Buy aggressively because the stock is about to break back into its former range.
B) Expect former support at ₹200 to act as a formidable new resistance ceiling where trapped buyers will sell to break even.
C) Ignore the ₹200 level because prior price history is deleted after a breakdown.
D) Polarity only applies in commodity markets, not equity stocks.

steps: 1. The Principle of Polarity is inviolable: broken support becomes resistance; broken resistance becomes support.
2. The greater the volume on a support breakdown, the stronger that level will act as overhead resistance.
3. The longer prices trade at a support or resistance zone, the more significant its role reversal becomes.
4. Trapped longs sell on the first return move to broken support to break even: use this as a short entry pivot.
5. Round numbers like $50, $100, and ₹1000 act as natural psychological stopping points for trend moves.
6. Never place stop-loss orders directly at round numbers; place them slightly above or below the psychological level.
7. Standard trend pullbacks predictably retrace 38.2%, 50%, or 61.8% of the preceding impulse wave.
8. A retracement exceeding 66% (or 61.8%) warns that the prior trend is undergoing a major structural reversal.
